About this citation

The text was assembled by Wang Yangming's disciples after his death and expanded over decades, so a numbered item belongs to a specific juan and edition. Wang's teaching reaches the reader here through his students' compilation rather than through anything he published.

Reading the cited source

The archive attributes this English wording to Instructions for Practical Living, Juan Shang and files it under Neo-Confucianism.

What a locator tells you, and what it does not · How this archive traces a quotation

About Wang Yangming

Wang Yangming (Wang Shouren, 1472–1529) was the Ming Neo-Confucian who taught unity of knowledge and action and innate moral knowing (liangzhi). A statesman and general who suppressed rebellions, he developed teachings in exile and military camps.

How to read this passage

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute. This passage enters that discussion through knowledge, practice.

Questions readers arrive with

What is the source of the quotation “Knowledge is the directing idea of action; action…”?

“Knowledge is the directing idea of action; action…” comes from Chuanxilu (Instructions for Practical Living), Juan Shang (Compiled from 1518; three-juan received edition 1556), attributed to Wang Yangming.

What does Wang Yangming mean by knowledge?

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute. This passage enters that discussion through knowledge, practice.
